mission.title: Install and Configure VMware Tanzu Kubernetes Grid
mission.description: VMware Tanzu Kubernetes Grid is a distribution that provides a robust framework for deploying and managing Kubernetes clusters in an enterprise environment. It leverages Carvel packaging and plugins for enhanced integration and user experience. Key trade-offs include the need for a more complex setup compared to simpler Kubernetes distributions, but it offers advanced features suitable for large-scale deployments.

steps.title: Install the Tanzu CLI
steps.description:
This step installs the Tanzu CLI, which is essential for managing Tanzu Kubernetes Grid.

```bash

curl -LO https://github.com/vmware-tanzu/tanzu-framework/releases/download/v0.29.0/tanzu-framework-linux-amd64.tar.gz

tar -xvf tanzu-framework-linux-amd64.tar.gz

sudo mv tanzu /usr/local/bin/

```

> Download the Tanzu CLI tarball.
> Extract the downloaded tarball.
> Move the Tanzu CLI to a directory in your PATH.

steps.title: Initialize the Tanzu CLI
steps.description:
This step initializes the Tanzu CLI and sets up the necessary configurations.

```bash

tanzu init

```

> Initialize the Tanzu CLI environment.

steps.title: Create a Tanzu Kubernetes Cluster
steps.description:
This step creates a new Tanzu Kubernetes cluster with specified parameters.

```bash

tanzu cluster create my-cluster --plan dev --kubernetes-version v1.29.0 --num-nodes 3 --region us-west-2

```

> Create a cluster named 'my-cluster' with 3 nodes.
commands: tanzu cluster create my-cluster --plan dev --kubernetes-version v1.29.0 --num-nodes 3 --region us-west-2

steps.title: Configure kubeconfig
steps.description:
This step configures the kubeconfig file to access the newly created cluster.

```bash

tanzu cluster kubeconfig get my-cluster --admin --context

```

> Get the kubeconfig for admin access to the cluster.

steps.title: Verify Cluster Nodes
steps.description:
This step verifies that the nodes in the cluster are up and running.

```bash

kubectl get nodes

```

> Check the status of the nodes in the cluster.

uninstall.title: Uninstall the Tanzu Kubernetes Cluster
uninstall.description:
This step removes the Tanzu Kubernetes cluster and may result in data loss. Ensure to backup any important data before proceeding.

```bash

tanzu cluster delete my-cluster

kubectl config delete-context my-cluster-admin@my-cluster

```

> Delete the cluster named 'my-cluster'.
> Remove the kubeconfig context for the deleted cluster.

upgrade.title: Upgrade the Tanzu Kubernetes Cluster
upgrade.description:
Before upgrading, ensure to backup your cluster data. This step upgrades the cluster to a newer version.

```bash

tanzu cluster backup my-cluster

tanzu cluster upgrade my-cluster --kubernetes-version v1.29.1

kubectl get nodes

```

> Backup the current state of the cluster.
> Upgrade the cluster to Kubernetes version 1.29.1.
> Verify that the nodes are running the new version.

troubleshooting.title: Error: Unable to connect to the cluster
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** The kubeconfig context may not be set correctly.

**Fix:**
Run 'kubectl config use-context my-cluster-admin@my-cluster' to set the correct context.

troubleshooting.title: Error: Cluster creation failed
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** Insufficient resources in the specified region.

**Fix:**
Check your cloud provider's resource availability and adjust the cluster specifications.

troubleshooting.title: Error: Nodes are in 'NotReady' state
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** The nodes may not have enough resources or may be misconfigured.

**Fix:**
Check node logs and ensure that the nodes meet the resource requirements.

troubleshooting.title: Error: Failed to retrieve cluster information
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** The cluster may not be initialized properly.

**Fix:**
Re-initialize the cluster using 'tanzu cluster create' and ensure all parameters are correct.

versionNotes.changes: Added support for Kubernetes 1.29, enhanced CLI commands for better usability.
versionNotes.deprecations: Deprecated older Kubernetes versions (1.26 and below).
versionNotes.migrationSteps: If upgrading from 2.4, ensure to backup your clusters and follow the upgrade commands.

resolution.summary: You should see the output of 'kubectl get nodes' displaying the nodes in 'Ready' state.
